name: Hadewijch
credit: Hadewijch's first strophic poem, 'Ay al es nu die winter cout', manuscript page (Ghent University Library, 14th c.) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Hadewijch was a Middle Dutch mystical writer and poet of the thirteenth century, probably from the Duchy of Brabant and perhaps a beguine. Nothing certain is known of her life beyond what her own writings suggest; she is usually dated to the middle of the century. She is the first great writer of Dutch mysticism.

Her works are the Visions, the Letters in prose, and two bodies of verse, the forty-five Strophic Poems and the Poems in Couplets. Her songs borrow the language of courtly love and the seasons of the troubadour tradition and turn it towards Minne, divine Love, in a poetry of longing, suffering and fulfilment.
